title: Runtime semver insurance policy and deprecation runway
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a prescriptive semantic versioning policy for the Redwood serving runtime together with LTS channel commitments, rollout gate definitions, and upgrade/migration tooling requirements. The goal is to provide 'insurance' that runtime evolution will not cause unexpected customer breakage while still allowing necessary improvements (optimizations, bugfixes, new features). The policy ties semantic versioning, deprecation headers, telemetry, and automated rollouts into a single operational playbook that platform teams, SDK maintainers, and customers can rely on. Outputs: (1) a concise semver policy document for runtime maintainers and SDKs, (2) deprecation header and warning format, (3) LTS lane definition and support windows, (4) rollout gate thresholds and automatic rollback criteria, and (5) upgrade tooling acceptance criteria (migration CLI, compatibility tests, adapter generator).
acceptance_criteria: A single-page semver policy describing what constitutes MAJOR, MINOR, and PATCH for the runtime and for public APIs
Deprecation header and warning format (HTTP header + structured JSON link) defined and documented
LTS lane support windows documented (active + security only) and mapping to release cadence
Rollout gate definitions implemented in the rollout operator and verified in a canary test run
Compatibility test harness that validates client adapters against new runtime versions included in CI
Migration tooling minimal prototype (migration-cli) that can generate suggested adapter shims from compatibility diffs
rollout_playbook: Canary rollout: initial 1% requests for 24h, then 10% for 24h, then 50% for 4h, full at 100% after health checks pass
Automatic rollback threshold: error-rate > 0.75% OR latency p95 regression > 30% sustained for 10 minutes triggers immediate rollback
Safe-mode: when rollback is impossible, runtime will enable compatibility-mode that forces backward-compatible behavior for known critical paths
Runtime exposes X-Runtime-Version and X-Runtime-Compatible headers; clients can opt into compatibility shims based on X-Runtime-Compatible
migration_tooling: migration-cli: proto to shim generator that reads compatibility diffs and spits out adapter suggestions
compat-check suite run in PRs: validates a matrix of SDK versions against the new runtime image in CI
adapter-generator: experimental tool to create lightweight runtime shims for common client incompatibilities
migration playbook docs and example PR templates for SDK maintainers and enterprise ops
telemetry_signals: consumer-impact-score (0-100) computed from error rate, client upgrade rate, and support tickets
unhandled-exception-rate per client-version reported to console and rollout operator
deprecation-warning-consumption: how many clients saw the header and executed a migration within 30 days
latency-percentile deltas per route, per model, per client-adapter
decisions: Adopt semver 2.0.0 for public runtime artifacts; MAJOR version bumps allowed only for changes that require client-side code modifications
MINOR releases may add non-breaking API improvements, new opt-in features, and performance improvements; PATCH for bugfixes and urgent security fixes
Introduce structured deprecation header: X-Deprecation-Info with fields 'deprecated_in', 'removal_date', 'migration_doc' (link) and 'severity'
Create an LTS lane with 12 months active support + 12 months security-only window; LTS releases numbered with suffix '.lts' and listed in console
All major changes require: compat-test pass, migration guide, and a migration-cli generated shim or explicit exemption with documented rationale
Rollout gates are enforced by the rollout operator; must be configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private customers
